STATEMENTS
Question 1 asks what personal characteristics define an excellent administrator. Godfrey answers that an excellent leader is often the determining factor within an organization, and that when an effort or team is headed by the right individual, time, resources and skills are maximized and people are empowered, inspired and productive. He identifies humility, integrity and vision as the three most important personal characteristics. He writes that educational leadership requires humility and a keen focus on service toward improving outcomes for learners, that selflessness and appreciation for collaboration are essential, and that servant leadership causes educators and stakeholders to sense their value and contribute toward common goals, whereas ego-driven leadership breeds competitive and hostile environments in which individuals fight for their own agendas rather than a shared vision. On integrity, he states it signals alignment between a leader's core beliefs and daily practice, that educational organizations have an implicit mandate to care for and nurture learners in environments fostering curiosity and inquiry, and that integrity in an educational leader translates to strong cultural values within the organization. On vision, he argues a concise, clearly communicated vision gives stakeholders a roadmap for navigating the changing landscape of education and prevents individuals and organizations from becoming sidetracked and discouraged by the perception or reality of wasted effort.

Question 2 asks how important technology is in education and what technology-related skills the applicant can contribute. Godfrey writes that 21st century learners have more information at their disposal than any generation before them, and that the expanding digital database of the internet can present as both gift and curse: the gift is access to worlds of knowledge at the click of a mouse or tap of a screen, which levels the playing field between educational haves and have nots, while the curse is the difficulty of filtering fact from fiction and truth from lies. His stated contributions are a healthy sense of perspective and an emphasis on critical thinking. He argues technology must remain a supplement to human understanding and connection rather than a replacement, comparing the Information Age to the eras revolutionized by the pencil and the printing press, and notes that the available wealth of knowledge includes voices previously stifled by oppressive and marginalizing forces. He concludes that when technology supplements critical thinking, learners add depth to breadth and learn to hold varying ideas in tension while remaining grounded in empirical truths.

2020_168_m111720bdmtg.paragraph: Minutes of the Troy Board of Education meeting held remotely via Zoom Webinar on November 17, 2020, called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m. and adjourned at 8:45 p.m. The Board approved a consent agenda, a $92,000 signage bid to Johnson Sign Company, a $1,687,276.00 school bus purchase from Hoekstra Transportation, monthly reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan on a 6-1 vote with Mrs. Hammond opposed, and a resolution urging the Legislature to amend Senate Bill 1108 of 2020 on remote meeting attendance.
2020_168_m111720bdmtg.page:
Meeting and Attendance
Troy Board of Education meeting, Troy, Michigan, November 17, 2020, held remotely via Zoom Webinar with public notice posted to allow remote community participation. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Present via Zoom in addition to Mr. Schmidt were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, Carrier, Griffor, DiPilato, Roncone, Haezebrouck, House, Pagel and West; two Student Board Reps; and approximately 48 additional members of the audience.

Recognition
TSD Mission Moment honoring Troy High School English teachers Jodie Duda, Erin Fischer-Ballew, Annie Gallagher, Christina Rick and Valerie Valentino, recipients of a Michigan Council of Teachers of English (MCTE) Diversity, Inclusion, Justice and Equity (DIJE) professional development grant. Their reading program includes Black Appetite. White Food by Jamila Lyiscott; We Got This. by Cornelius Miner; The Anti-Racist Teacher: Reading Instruction Workbook by Lorena German; Educating Activist Allies by Katy Swalwell; and Linguistic Justice by April Baker-Bell.

Public Communication
There were no additions or deletions. Andrew Rodman, Troy resident and parent of two Martell Elementary School students, addressed the Board about the decision to move elementary students back to remote learning and when they plan to return to in-seat. No one spoke during non-agenda public communication.

Actions
| No. | Item | Mover / Support | Vote |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20-084 | Consent agenda items A, B, C | Hauff / Hammond | 7-0 |
| 20-085 | Building signage award, Johnson Sign Company, $92,000 | Anne / Philippart | 7-0 |
| 20-086 | Bus purchase, Hoekstra Transportation, $1,687,276.00 | Philippart / Anne | 7-0 |
| 20-087 | Reconfirmation of COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan | Wilson / Philippart | 6-1, Hammond No |
| 20-088 | Open Meetings Act resolution on Senate Bill 1108 | Philippart / Hauff | 7-0 |

The consent agenda covered minutes of the October 6, 2020 Board Workshop, minutes of the October 20, 2020 Board Meeting, and the Treasurer's Report for September 2020. The signage award covers refurbishment of the school messaging sign at Athens High School and new messaging signs at the Troy Preschool and Troy Learning Center, inclusive of 6% contingency, charged to the 2019 Capital Projects Fund and/or the Sinking Fund. The bus award is charged to the 2019 Capital Projects Fund; discussion covered bus end-of-life cycle and resale value, and grants for electric buses, which Mr. West explained would be cost-prohibitive at this time.

Other Business
Dr. Machesky presented an update on the District's extended learning plan with PowerPoint slides on climbing COVID case counts in Michigan and Oakland County, with additional updates from Ms. Birmingham, Mrs. Griffor and Mrs. DiPilato. The COVID-19 plan reconfirmation follows Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142, which requires monthly board reconfirmation and website posting. The Open Meetings Act resolution addresses Senate Bill 1108 of 2020 and directs transmittal within five business days to Senator Mallory McMorrow, Representative Padma Kuppa, Oakland Schools Intermediate School District, and the Michigan Association of School Boards.

Comments and Adjournment
Board comments came from Hammond, Wilson, Philippart (TFEE raffle for $1,000 worth of gift cards, tickets $5 each), Gottlieb, Hauff and Anne. Student representatives Pranay Gupta (International Academy - East) and Nathania Nartey (Athens High School) reported; Sejal Patel and Carleton Thomas were not in attendance. Dr. Machesky congratulated Bemis Elementary School on National Blue Ribbon recognition for the second time. Mr. Schmidt announced the next Board Workshop for December 1st at 6:00 p.m. via Zoom. Adjourned at 8:45 p.m.; minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary.
2020_168_m111720bdmtg.verbose:
Minutes of the Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, Board Meeting of November 17, 2020, held via Zoom Webinar. The meeting was held remotely and a public notice was posted in order to allow community members to participate remotely. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present via Zoom videoconference were Board members Anne, Gottlieb, Hammond, Hauff, Philippart and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky; administrators Birmingham, Carrier, Griffor, DiPilato, Roncone, Haezebrouck, House, Pagel and West; two Student Board Reps; and approximately 48 additional members of the audience.

RECOGNITION - TSD MISSION MOMENT
The Michigan Council of Teachers of English (MCTE) Diversity, Inclusion, Justice, and Equity (DIJE) subcommittee awarded Jodie Duda, Erin Fischer-Ballew, Annie Gallagher, Christina Rick, and Valerie Valentino of Troy High School a DIJE professional development grant. The stated goal of the grant is to support Michigan English teachers across the state as they engage in professional development they design that privileges diversity, inclusion, justice, and equity work. The recipients created a program of reading and learning supporting their commitment to disrupting stock stories, stereotypes, and westernized narratives. Their selected texts are Black Appetite. White Food: Issues of Race, Voice and Justice Within and Beyond the Classroom, by Jamila Lyiscott; We Got This.: Equity, Access, and the Quest to Be Who Our Students Need Us to Be, by Cornelius Miner; The Anti-Racist Teacher: Reading Instruction Workbook, by Lorena German; Educating Activist Allies: Social Justice Pedagogy with the Suburban and Urban Elite, by Katy Swalwell; and Linguistic Justice: Black Language, Literacy, Identity, and Pedagogy, by April Baker-Bell. Their intention is to use the concepts and practice presented in their readings to plan learning for their students to build community and engage in rich activist lives.

ADDITIONS AND DELETIONS
None.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION
Andrew Rodman, Troy resident and parent of two students who attend Martell Elementary School, addressed the Board about the decision to move elementary students back to remote learning and when they plan to return to in-seat.

GENERAL - CONSENT AGENDA (Resolution 20-084)
It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mrs. Hammond that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, and C on the consent agenda: minutes of the October 6, 2020 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the October 20, 2020 Board of Education Meeting; and the Treasurer's Report for September 2020. On roll call vote, Schmidt Yes, Wilson Yes, Anne Yes, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond Yes, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PERSONNEL AND CURRICULUM
No items were recorded under Personnel or Curriculum.

BUSINESS - BUILDING SIGNAGE (Resolution 20-085)
It was moved by Mrs. Anne and supported by Dr. Philippart that the bid for signage for the refurbishment of the school messaging sign at Athens High School and new messaging signs at the Troy Preschool and Troy Learning Center be awarded to Johnson Sign Company in the amount of $92,000 (inclusive of 6% contingency), and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund and/or the Sinking Fund. On roll call vote, Wilson Yes, Anne Yes, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond Yes, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes, Schmidt Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BUSINESS - BUS PURCHASE (Resolution 20-086)
It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mrs. Anne that the bid for school buses be awarded to Hoekstra Transportation in the amount of $1,687,276.00 and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2019 Capital Projects Fund. There was discussion about the end of life cycle for buses and how much money the District could sell them for. There was also discussion about looking into grants for electric buses; however, Mr. West explained that it would be cost-prohibitive at this time. On roll call vote, Anne Yes, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond Yes, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes, Schmidt Yes, Wilson Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION - NON-AGENDA ITEMS
None.

OTHER - EXTENDED LEARNING PLAN
Dr. Machesky shared an update on the District's extended learning plan and provided PowerPoint slides showing the most recent numbers in COVID cases and how much they had been climbing in Michigan and in Oakland County. Ms. Birmingham, Mrs. Griffor and Mrs. DiPilato also shared updates from their respective areas, and there was further discussion among Board members.

RECONFIRMATION OF COVID-19 PREPAREDNESS AND RESPONSE PLAN (Resolution 20-087)
The minutes recite that Governor Whitmer's Executive Order 2020-142 provides a structure to support all schools in Michigan as they plan for a return of Pre-K through Post High School education in the fall, and that under this order Michigan school districts must adopt a COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan laying out how they will cope with the disease across the various phases of the Michigan Safe Start Plan. Each district must submit a reconfirmation plan to its Board of Education for approval on a monthly basis, and once approved must post its Preparedness Plan on the district website home page for public access. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Dr. Philippart that the Troy Board of Education approve the District's Reconfirmation of the COVID-19 Preparedness and Response Plan. On roll call vote, Gottlieb Yes, Hammond No, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes, Schmidt Yes, Wilson Yes, Anne Yes. Yes: 6, No: 1.

OPEN MEETINGS ACT RESOLUTION (Resolution 20-088)
It was moved by Dr. Philippart and supported by Mr. Hauff. The whereas clauses state that Michigan Senate Bill 1108 of 2020 amended the State's Open Meetings Act to restrict the reasons a member of a public body may attend a public meeting remotely beginning January 1, 2021; that advancing technology enabled school districts across the State to meet remotely during the COVID-19 pandemic, to develop and implement plans to educate students safely and effectively, and to ensure safe and effective public participation; that the restrictions in Senate Bill 1108 allow remote attendance after December 31, 2021 only for absence due to military duty; that threats to public health and other disasters will not vanish on December 31, 2020, and that contagious diseases, flooding, tornadoes, acts of terrorism or other causes occurring after that date could make it unsafe or impossible for public bodies to meet in person or for some members to attend in person; that not allowing an immune-compromised member of a public body to participate remotely would be a clear violation of the Reasonable Accommodation clause of the Federal Americans with Disabilities Act; and that decisions about situations that may or may not merit remote attendance by members of a local public body are best determined by that body and the community it represents rather than the State Legislature.

The resolved clauses urge the Legislature to ideally amend Senate Bill 1108, Sec. 3a(b) to include a provision requiring local public bodies to set their own policies regarding remote meeting participation based on the needs and priorities of their own local communities rather than dictating universal policy to all public bodies in the State without regard to local control; urge the Legislature at a minimum to amend Senate Bill 1108, Sec. 3a(b) to extend indefinitely its provisions allowing remote attendance to accommodate absence due to a medical condition or a statewide or local state of emergency or state of disaster, in addition to military service, and to add accommodations for family emergencies and work obligations; and direct the Board Secretary to transmit copies of the resolution within five business days of adoption to Senator Mallory McMorrow, Representative Padma Kuppa, Oakland Schools Intermediate School District, and the Michigan Association of School Boards. On roll call vote, Hammond Yes, Hauff Yes, Philippart Yes, Schmidt Yes, Wilson Yes, Anne Yes, Gottlieb Yes. Yes: 7, No: 0.

BOARD COMMENTS
Mrs. Hammond spoke about the events that happened during the last Board meeting, said how unfair it was presented, and stated that she will continue to advocate for what she believes in. Dr. Wilson thanked the teachers and administrators for their hard work in making things go as smoothly as possible. Dr. Philippart announced that the TFEE is holding a pandemic-safe fundraiser offering a raffle for $1,000 worth of gift cards, with tickets available for $5 each. Mr. Gottlieb thanked the TSD staff and fellow board members for all they are doing during these trying times. Mr. Hauff thanked veterans for their sacrifice and service, thanked the Central Office staff and hardworking teachers, and said oneTROY is the greatest school district in Michigan. Mrs. Anne thanked everyone for all they are doing during these difficult times.

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES
Pranay Gupta, student representative from International Academy - East, reported on what is happening with students learning virtually in his school. Nathania Nartey, student representative from Athens High School, reported on what is happening with students now that they are 100% virtual. Sejal Patel, student representative from Troy High School, was not in attendance. Carleton Thomas, student representative from Troy College and Career High School, was not in attendance.

ADJOURNMENT
Dr. Machesky thanked the Board for their continued efforts to support the District's work and for their help in supporting the LIVE program. He congratulated Bemis Elementary School for being recognized as a National Blue Ribbon School for the second time and wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving. Mr. Schmidt wished everyone a Happy Thanksgiving and announced that the next Board Workshop would be held on December 1st at 6:00 p.m. via Zoom. The meeting was adjourned at 8:45 p.m. The minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the preparation notation GH/jh.
